answer.summary: Norton recommends treating people-side leadership as a core, trainable part of product management and deliberately practicing it from day one, even without formal authority.

sections.heading: Treat people skills as essential skills to develop
sections.content: Don’t dismiss communication, collaboration, and other people skills as merely “soft” or assume they aren’t trainable. Norton says to invest in them as deliberately as in product techniques such as backlog management—and recognizes that over time they may be just as important or more important.

sections.heading: Practice leadership without formal authority
sections.content: Start from day one: PMs are expected to lead even though they are nobody’s boss. Use that role to sharpen leadership skills and intuitions by practicing how to persuade people, bring groups together to work, handle difficult personalities, set and articulate a vision, and create an environment where people can collaborate and play.
